mainTopic: רבי אלעזר's ban on ייבום after a divorce and remarriage, and two brothers married to two sisters who are minors
overview: The משנה ends its cases of a man who divorced his wife, took her back, and died childless. The רבנן allow ייבום and רבי אלעזר forbids it, but everyone forbids it for a קטנה married off by her father who was divorced and then remarried. The גמרא looks for רבי אלעזר's reason. עיפה's answer is rejected. אביי says רבי אלעזר is unsure whether death or the first marriage links her to the יבם. רבא says it is a safeguard because people may not know about the remarriage. רב אשי says it is a decree because of the remarried minor 'orphan in her father's lifetime,' and the משנה and a ברייתא support him. רב נחמן rules that her צרה may still do ייבום, since we do not make a גזירה לגזירה. A new משנה discusses two brothers married to two sisters who are minors or deaf-mutes. When the adult sister is widowed, רבי אליעזר, רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע give three different solutions. The גמרא defends teaching a minor to do מיאון when it is for a מצוה, and then begins explaining בר קפרא's list of things to cling to.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר disagrees, and the orphan girl case
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends the previous case with רבי אלעזר's dissent. It then adds a parallel case: an orphan girl who was divorced and taken back is permitted to the יבם, and again רבי אלעזר forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר forbids it. Likewise, if a man divorces an orphan girl and then takes her back, she is permitted to the יבם, and רבי אלעזר forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a list of cases where a husband divorced his wife, remarried her, and then died childless. Each time the main opinion permits ייבום and רבי אלעזר forbids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case, a man who divorced his own wife and took her back, began on the previous דף. The orphan here is a girl married off by her mother or brothers after her father died, so her marriage is only from the רבנן. Even so, the same dispute applies to her: permitted according to the main opinion, forbidden according to רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: forbids
one who divorces
an orphan girl (here, a minor whose father has died)
and he took her back (remarried her)
the brother-in-law who may do ייבום

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar prohibits.
phrases.notes: This finishes the case from the previous דף: a man who divorced his wife, took her back, and then died.

phrases.english: And likewise, one who divorces the orphan girl
and took her back: she is permitted to the yavam.
And Rabbi Elazar prohibits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A divorced and remarried wife, including a remarried orphan girl, is permitted to the יבם according to the main opinion. רבי אלעזר forbids her.

steps.title: A minor married off by her father: everyone forbids
steps.stepSummary: A קטנה married off by her father and then divorced is like an orphan in her father's lifetime. If her husband takes her back, everyone agrees she is forbidden to the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: A minor girl whose father married her off, and who was then divorced, is like an orphan while her father is alive. If her husband takes her back, everyone agrees she is forbidden to the יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case where even the main opinion agrees that ייבום is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her first marriage, arranged by her father, was a full Torah marriage, and the divorce ended it. After the divorce, her father can no longer marry her off, and a minor cannot make a full marriage herself, so she is 'like an orphan.' Her second marriage to the same man is therefore weaker than the first, and here everyone agrees she is forbidden to the יבם.

keyTerms.meaning: a minor girl
whose father married her off
like an orphan during her father's lifetime
everyone agrees

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this girl with the orphan in the previous step. The orphan's first marriage was only from the רבנן, but this girl's first marriage was a full Torah marriage. That difference is why everyone forbids here.

phrases.english: A minor girl whose father married her off,
and she was divorced: she is like an orphan in the father's lifetime.
phrases.notes: Once she is divorced, her father can no longer marry her off, so she is in the same position as an orphan.

phrases.english: And if he took her back, all agree she is forbidden to the yavam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case where the dispute disappears and everyone forbids.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor married off by her father, divorced, and then taken back is forbidden to the יבם according to everyone.

steps.title: Eifa's reason for רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: עיפה explains that רבי אלעזר forbids ייבום because the woman was forbidden to the brother for a time, while she was divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: עיפה said: What is רבי אלעזר's reason? Since she was forbidden to him for one moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking why רבי אלעזר forbids ייבום, and עיפה offers an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While she was divorced, she was simply the brother's ex-wife, who is forbidden to him. עיפה argues that once she was forbidden to the יבם at some point, ייבום can never permit her, even after she was remarried.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה
a sage of the גמרא
what is the reason?
since, because
she was forbidden to him for one moment

phrases.english: Gemara:
Eifa said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Elazar?
Since she stood before him
phrases.notes: The time she was divorced, when she was just his brother's ex-wife and forbidden to him.

phrases.english: one moment in a state of prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עֵיפָה: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי אלעזר's opinion in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because she was forbidden to the יבם for a time, ייבום cannot permit her.

steps.title: Then she shouldn't need חליצה either
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן challenge עיפה: if she is fully forbidden to the יבם, she should not need חליצה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to עיפה: If so, she should not need חליצה either!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן attack עיפה's explanation by pointing out what it would lead to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who is truly forbidden to the יבם is completely outside ייבום, so she needs no חליצה either. If עיפה's reason were correct, she would be fully exempt from both, which would be a surprising result.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sages
if so
the ceremony that releases a widow from ייבום
she should need

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Eifa:
If so,
she should not need chalitza either!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְעֵיפָה: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עיפה's reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: עיפה's explanation that she was forbidden for a time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A woman truly forbidden to the יבם needs no חליצה, so עיפה's reason would exempt her from חליצה too.

steps.title: A ברייתא says רבי אלעזר requires חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes off a possible defense. One might answer that רבי אלעזר really does exempt her from חליצה, but a ברייתא quotes him saying she does חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that is indeed so, wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: They said in the name of רבי אלעזר that she does חליצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the easy way out of the challenge in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עיפה could have accepted the result and said she needs no חליצה. The ברייתא shows that רבי אלעזר himself requires חליצה, so עיפה's reason cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you would say
indeed so
she does חליצה

phrases.english: And if you say: indeed so,
phrases.notes: He means: maybe רבי אלעזר really does say she needs no חליצה.

phrases.english: but wasn't it taught in a baraita:
They said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: she does chalitza!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge by ruling out the possible defense.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible defense that רבי אלעזר exempts her from חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא records that רבי אלעזר requires חליצה, so that defense fails.

steps.title: Eifa admits he doesn't know the reason
steps.stepSummary: עיפה withdraws his explanation and admits that he does not know רבי אלעזר's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, עיפה said: As for רבי אלעזר, I do not know what his reason is.
steps.whatsHappening: עיפה's attempt ends here. He takes back his answer, which leaves the question open for the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one has an explanation that fits both of רבי אלעזר's rulings: no ייבום, but חליצה is still required. The question is now open again, and that sets up אביי's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (taking back what came before)
I do not know

phrases.english: Rather, Eifa said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לָא יָדַעְנָא מַאי טַעְמָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar: I do not know what his reason is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives in to the challenge.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עיפה's reason is rejected, and רבי אלעזר's reason is still unknown.

steps.title: אביי: רבי אלעזר is unsure what makes her fall to ייבום
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that רבי אלעזר is unsure whether the brother's death or the original marriage is what makes her fall to the יבם. If it is death, she is fit for ייבום. If it is the original marriage, she was forbidden for a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is רבי אלעזר's reason. He is unsure whether death makes her fall to the יבם, or the first marriage does. If death does, she stands before him ready for ייבום. If the first marriage does, she was forbidden to him for a moment.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new explanation of רבי אלעזר that fits both rulings: no ייבום, but חליצה is still needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bond with the יבם is created at the moment of death, she was the brother's wife at that moment and is fit for ייבום. If the bond is created by the original marriage, it was broken by the divorce while she was forbidden, and she is out. Because רבי אלעזר is unsure, he holds there is no ייבום, but she still needs חליצה, which answers the רבנן's challenge to עיפה.

keyTerms.meaning: he is unsure
death makes her fall (to the יבם)
the original marriage
she lies before him for ייבום

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, רבי אלעזר is unsure whether death or the original marriage creates the link to the יבם. That doubt explains both of his rulings: no ייבום, yet חליצה is required.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question of whether death or the original marriage creates the link to the יבם is a basic idea in the laws of ייבום.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Abaye said: This is the reason of Rabbi Elazar:
He is unsure whether death makes her fall,
phrases.notes: 'Fall' means fall to the יבם, becoming bound to him for ייבום.

phrases.english: or whether the original marriage makes her fall.
If death makes her fall,
then she lies before him for yibum,
if the original marriage makes her fall,

phrases.aramaic: הָא עָמְדָה עָלָיו שָׁעָה אַחַת בְּאִיסּוּר.
phrases.english: then she stood before him one moment in prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question עיפה could not answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads רבי אלעזר's ruling as based on doubt rather than a definite prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עיפה thought she was definitely forbidden, so she would need no חליצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is forbidden only out of doubt, so there is no ייבום but she still needs חליצה.

steps.title: רבא: The worry is that people do not know about the remarriage
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי אלעזר agrees death decides that she falls to the יבם. He forbids ייבום only because people know about the divorce but may not know about the remarriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, רבי אלעזר is sure that death is what makes her fall to the יבם. But everyone knows about divorces, while not everyone knows about remarriages.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new reason for רבי אלעזר, different from אביי's doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, רבי אלעזר has no doubt at all. By Torah law the woman would be fit for ייבום, because death decides. The ban is a safeguard. People remember the divorce but may have missed the remarriage, so they could think the brother married his brother's divorcee, which is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: death is what makes her fall to the יבם
well-informed, aware
divorce
remarriage to the same husband

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is NOT saying she is truly forbidden by Torah law. He agrees she is fit for ייבום. The ban only exists so that people will not get the wrong idea.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Actually, it is obvious to Rabbi Elazar
phrases.notes: He is answering אביי, who said רבי אלעזר was unsure. רבא says he wasn't unsure at all.

phrases.english: that death is what makes her fall [to the yavam],
however, everyone is aware of divorces,
but not everyone is aware of remarriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם פְּשִׁיטָא לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְּמִיתָה מַפֶּלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation from אביי's. It rejects the idea that רבי אלעזר is in doubt.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר was unsure whether death or the original marriage decides (אביי).
steps.terutzMaskana: Death clearly decides. The ban is a decree because people may not know about the remarriage.

steps.title: But a remarriage is public
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רבא: a remarriage becomes well known, because she lives with him again.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: a remarriage, since she lives with him, becomes publicly known!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's claim that people will not know about the remarriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's whole reason depends on people not knowing about the remarriage. The גמרא argues the opposite. Once she is living in his house again, everyone sees it, so there should be no confusion.

keyTerms.meaning: on the contrary
she lives with him (literally, sits under him)
publicity, a known report

phrases.english: On the contrary:
remarriage, since she lives with him,
becomes publicly known!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה: חֲזָרָה, כֵּיוָן דְּיָתְבָא תּוּתֵיהּ, אִית לֵיהּ קָלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the factual basis of רבא's explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that not everyone knows about the remarriage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Living together again is visible to everyone, so the remarriage should be at least as well known as the divorce.

steps.title: He may have remarried her at night and died in the morning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רבא: sometimes the remarriage is too short for anyone to notice, such as when he remarried her in the evening and died the next morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are we not also dealing with a case where he remarried her in the evening and died in the morning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to a case where the remarriage would not become known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Living together makes a remarriage public only if it lasts a while. If the husband died right after remarrying her, people never found out. They would think the brother married a divorcee. רבי אלעזר made one rule that covers every case, so that such situations never happen.

keyTerms.meaning: are we not dealing with (a case where)…
evening
morning

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, death clearly makes her fall to the יבם. רבי אלעזר forbids her only so that people who missed a short remarriage do not get confused.

phrases.english: Are we not dealing [also with a case]
where he remarried her in the evening
and died in the morning?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא עָסְקִינַן דְּאַהְדְּרַהּ בְּאוּרְתָּא וּשְׁכֵיב בְּצַפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 and saves רבא's explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a case where the challenge does not apply
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every remarriage becomes public, so there is no room for confusion.
steps.terutzMaskana: A very short remarriage stays unknown. So רבי אלעזר forbids every case.

steps.title: רב אשי: A decree because of the minor 'orphan in her father's lifetime'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says רבי אלעזר forbade every divorced-and-remarried woman because of one specific case: a minor girl who is like an orphan in her father's lifetime and was remarried.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This is רבי אלעזר's reason. He made a decree about these women because of an 'orphan in her father's lifetime' whom the husband remarried.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a third explanation. It is a rabbinic decree based on a related case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A minor girl who was married off by her father and then divorced is like an orphan. If her husband remarries her, that second marriage is only rabbinic, so she is truly forbidden to the יבם. To keep people from mixing up the two cases, רבי אלעזר forbade every woman who was divorced and remarried.

keyTerms.meaning: he made a rabbinic decree
a minor girl treated like an orphan even though her father is alive
and he remarried her

steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the source of רבי אלעזר's ruling away from Torah logic. It becomes a rabbinic decree that protects a related case where she really is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
This is the reason of Rabbi Elazar:
he made a decree about these
phrases.notes: 'These' are ordinary women whose husbands divorced them and then remarried them.

phrases.english: because of an 'orphan in her father's lifetime' whom he remarried.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, independent explanation of רבי אלעזר, different from those of אביי and רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic decree based on a related case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's reason comes from doubt (אביי) or from public confusion about the remarriage (רבא).
steps.terutzMaskana: He decreed against all remarried divorcees because of the minor 'orphan' who was remarried.

steps.title: Support from the סיפא of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support for רב אשי from the last clause of the משנה. There, a minor who was divorced and remarried is forbidden to the יבם according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also reasonable, from what the latter clause teaches: A minor girl whose father married her off and who was divorced is like an orphan in her father's lifetime. If he remarried her, all agree she is forbidden to the יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the סיפא of the משנה to set up a proof for רב אשי. The proof is completed in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא describes exactly the case רב אשי pointed to. Placing this case right next to רבי אלעזר's ruling hints that the two are connected. The real force of the proof comes in steps 13 and 14.

keyTerms.meaning: so too it is reasonable (a supporting proof)
the latter clause of a משנה
a minor girl
all opinions agree

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
from what is taught in the latter clause:
A minor girl whose father married her off and who was divorced
is like an orphan in her father's lifetime.
phrases.notes: Once she is divorced, her father can no longer marry her off, so she is like a girl with no father.

phrases.english: And if he remarried her
all agree that she is forbidden to the yavam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a proof for רב אשי's explanation.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that רבי אלעזר's decree is based on the minor orphan case
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה about the minor who was divorced and remarried

steps.title: Why would the משנה state something obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the סיפא needs to teach this ruling, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of saying this? It is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a pointed question that sets up the conclusion of the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A minor's remarriage is only rabbinic. So once she is divorced, she is clearly a divorcee of the dead brother and forbidden to the יבם. Because the ruling is so plain, it must be in the משנה to teach something extra.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the point of saying this?
it is obvious

phrases.english: What is the point of saying this?
It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds the proof by showing that the סיפא seems unnecessary.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the משנה need to teach that the remarried minor orphan is forbidden to the יבם?

steps.title: The סיפא teaches רבי אלעזר's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the סיפא is there to show the reason behind רבי אלעזר's ruling. He decreed against all remarried divorcees because of the minor orphan case. This proves רב אשי right.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not teaching us this: the reason of רבי אלעזר is that he decreed against those women because of this one. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question and closes the proof for רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'obvious' ruling in the סיפא actually explains the רישא. The case where she is truly forbidden, the remarried minor, is the reason רבי אלעזר also forbids ordinary remarried divorcees. The words שמע מינה confirm that רב אשי's explanation is supported by the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it teaches us
learn from it (the proof stands)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, רבי אלעזר's ban is a rabbinic decree. Ordinary remarried divorcees are forbidden to the יבם so they will not be confused with a remarried minor 'orphan,' who really is forbidden. The משנה's סיפא proves it.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן,
phrases.english: Rather, is it not teaching us this:
the reason of Rabbi Elazar
is that he decreed against those because of this one.
phrases.notes: 'Those' are ordinary remarried divorcees. 'This one' is the minor orphan from the סיפא.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 and completes the proof begun in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה supports רב אשי: רבי אלעזר forbade remarried divorcees as a decree because of the remarried minor orphan.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the חכמים agree with רבי אלעזר about a minor who is like an orphan in her father's lifetime and was remarried. She is forbidden to the יבם, because her divorce was complete and her remarriage was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רב אשי. The חכמים agree with רבי אלעזר about a minor girl whose father married her off and who was then divorced. She is now like an orphan in her father's lifetime. If her husband remarried her, she is forbidden to the יבם. This is because her divorce was a complete divorce, but her remarriage was not a complete remarriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב אשי's explanation of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא names the exact case רב אשי pointed to, a minor who is like an orphan in her father's lifetime. Her divorce counts fully, but her remarriage as a minor counts only partly. So when her husband dies, she is treated like a divorcee of the brother, who is forbidden to the יבם. That is the problem that led רבי אלעזר to his decree.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא is taught that agrees with him
An 'orphan in her father's lifetime': a girl whose father can no longer marry her off
A complete, fully valid divorce
A complete, fully valid remarriage
The dead husband's brother, who may do יבום or חליצה

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא confirms the conclusion from step 14. רבי אלעזר's general decree is rooted in this one specific minor's case.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with Rav Ashi:
The Rabbis agree with Rabbi Elazar
about a minor girl whose father married her off and who was then divorced
she is like an orphan in her father's lifetime,
phrases.notes: Her father can't marry her off again, so like a real orphan she can only marry by rabbinic law.

phrases.english: and her husband remarried her
that she is forbidden to the yavam,
because her divorce was a complete divorce,
but her remarriage is not a complete remarriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא as further support for the conclusion reached in step 14
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that רבי אלעזר's decree comes from the case of a minor who is like an orphan in her father's lifetime
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that the חכמים agree with רבי אלעזר in that exact case

steps.title: The agreement applies only if she was a minor at both stages
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the agreement to a girl divorced and remarried while still a minor. If she was remarried as an adult, or grew up while married to him, she may do either חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this ruling apply? Only when he divorced her while she was a minor and remarried her while she was still a minor. But suppose he divorced her as a minor and remarried her as an adult. Or suppose he remarried her as a minor, she grew up while married to him, and then he died. In those cases she may do either חליצה or יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and limits the ruling it just gave to one narrow case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is only an incomplete remarriage. If she was an adult when remarried, the remarriage is fully valid. If she grew up while living with him, the marriage becomes fully valid too. Either way she is a regular widow, so the חכמים allow יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (a limiting formula)
An adult girl, past the age of a minor
She grew up while married to him
She does חליצה
She does יבום (marries the יבם)

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
Where he divorced her while she was a minor
and remarried her while she was a minor.
But if he divorced her while she was a minor
and remarried her when she was an adult,
or if he remarried her while she was a minor
and she grew up while with him, and he died
she may either do chalitza or do yibum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the agreement in step 15 to a girl who was a minor at both the divorce and the remarriage
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the חכמים' view, only a remarriage done entirely while she was a minor forbids her. If she was an adult by the remarriage, or matured during it, she may do חליצה or יבום.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר still requires חליצה in those cases
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רבי אלעזר they said: even in those cases she does חליצה and not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of רבי אלעזר they said: she does חליצה and may not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבי אלעזר's view. Even when the remarriage was fully valid, she still may not do יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows רבי אלעזר made a broad decree. Because of the minor's case, he forbade יבום for every divorced-and-remarried woman, even where her own marriage was complete. That is exactly what רב אשי said in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: They said in the name of רבי אלעזר
And she does not do יבום

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים forbid יבום only in the true minor case. רבי אלעזר extends this to all remarried divorcees as a protective decree.

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Elazar they said:
She does chalitza and does not do yibum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי אלעזר's dissent from the leniency in step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר, any divorced-and-remarried woman does חליצה and not יבום, even if her remarriage was fully valid.

steps.title: רבא asks about the rival wife
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן what the law is for the צרה of this woman, according to רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: What is the law for her rival wife?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question. Does רבי אלעזר's decree also stop her צרה from doing יבום?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when a woman is forbidden to the יבם as an ערוה, her צרה is also exempt. רבא wants to know whether this woman, forbidden only by decree, is treated strongly enough to affect her צרה too.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him
Her rival wife: the other wife of the same dead husband
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Nachman:
Her rival wife, what is her law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי אלעזר's decree and asks how far it reaches
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the צרה of a divorced-and-remarried woman is also barred from יבום under רבי אלעזר's decree

steps.title: No decree on top of a decree
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the woman herself is forbidden only by a decree. We do not add another decree on top of that to forbid her צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: She herself is forbidden only because of a decree. Should we now go and make a decree to protect a decree?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא. The צרה is permitted to do יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman herself is not forbidden by the Torah. Her ban is only a rabbinic safeguard. Forbidding her צרה would mean adding a second safeguard on top of the first, which the חכמים do not do.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
A decree to protect a decree, which we do not make
She herself

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'we do not make a גזירה לגזירה' is a basic limit on rabbinic decrees that appears across ש״ס.

phrases.english: He said to him:
She herself is forbidden only by a decree,
and shall we get up and make a decree to protect a decree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question from step 18
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The צרה is permitted to do יבום, because her co-wife is forbidden only by decree, and we do not make a גזירה לגזירה.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to include the rival wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן with a ברייתא in רבי אלעזר's name: 'She and her rival wife do חליצה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: In the name of רבי אלעזר they said: She and her rival wife do חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן's answer. A ברייתא seems to say that the צרה also needs חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the צרה must do חליצה, then she is barred from יבום, just like the woman herself. That contradicts רב נחמן's ruling that the צרה is allowed יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge)
She and her rival wife

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
In the name of Rabbi Elazar they said:
She and her rival wife do chalitza.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנְיָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's answer in step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the צרה may do יבום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא in רבי אלעזר's name puts the צרה together with the woman for חליצה. That suggests the צרה may not do יבום.

steps.title: The ברייתא must mean one or the other
steps.stepSummary: The wording 'she and her rival' cannot be literal, since only one wife needs חליצה. So the ברייתא must mean 'either she or her rival does חליצה,' and neither does יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could you really think 'she and her rival wife' both do חליצה? Rather, doesn't it mean that either she or her rival wife does חליצה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens its challenge. It explains how the ברייתא must be read, and that reading still goes against רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both wives cannot need חליצה. Once one wife does חליצה, all the wives of that brother are free. So the ברייתא must mean that one of them does חליצה, whichever it is. Either way, no יבום is allowed, which still bars the צרה from יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (this cannot be right)
Rather, isn't it...? (offers the forced reading)

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not reject the challenge. It shows that even with the wording fixed, the ברייתא still seems to bar the צרה from יבום.

phrases.english: 'She and her rival wife,' could that enter your mind?!
phrases.notes: One wife's chalitza frees all the brother's wives, so both of them can't need chalitza.

phrases.english: Rather, doesn't it mean:
either she or her rival wife does chalitza?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fixes the wording of the ברייתא from step 20 so the challenge can stand
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the צרה may do יבום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read correctly, the ברייתא says one of the two wives must do חליצה, with no יבום for either. So the צרה is also barred from יבום.

steps.title: Fix the wording a different way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: if the ברייתא's wording needs fixing anyway, fix it so that she does חליצה, while her צרה may do either חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Aren't you fixing the wording anyway? Then fix it this way: she does חליצה, and her rival wife may do either חליצה or יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן. It offers a different correction of the ברייתא that fits his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the ברייתא cannot be read exactly as written. So there is no reason to prefer the challenger's correction. A correction that permits the צרה fits the rule against a גזירה לגזירה, so רב נחמן's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: You are already fixing the wording
Fix it this way

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, the divorced-and-remarried woman herself does only חליצה. Her צרה may do חליצה or יבום, because we do not make a גזירה לגזירה.

phrases.english: Aren't you fixing the wording anyway?
Fix it this way:
She does chalitza,
her rival wife may either do chalitza or do yibum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 20-21 by offering another correction of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא must mean either wife does חליצה, so neither may do יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means she does חליצה, and her צרה may do חליצה or יבום. This fits רב נחמן.

steps.title: Two brothers married to two minor sisters, and the simple cases
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that when two brothers are married to two minor sisters and one brother dies, the widow goes out as אחות אשה. The same applies to two deaf-mute sisters, and to an adult and a minor when the minor's husband dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Two brothers are married to two sisters who are both minors, and the husband of one of them died. This widow goes out, because she is the sister of his wife. The same is true of two deaf-mute sisters. If one sister is an adult and one is a minor, and the minor's husband died, the minor goes out, because she is the sister of his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It lays out the easy cases, where the widow is simply exempt because she is the living brother's wife's sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each of these cases the widow's own marriage to the dead brother was only rabbinic, so her bond of יבום is weak. The living brother's wife counts as his wife at least as strongly as that bond. So the widow is treated as אחות אשה and goes out with no יבום at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the base text the גמרא discusses
A wife's sister, whom a man may not marry while his wife is alive
A minor girl; her marriage (arranged after her father's death) is only valid by rabbinic law
A deaf-mute woman; her marriage is also only rabbinic
She goes out: she is free without יבום

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the widow here needs חליצה. 'תֵּצֵא' means she is fully exempt, with no יבום and no חליצה, just like any ערוה.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Two brothers who are married
to two sisters who are minors,
and the husband of one of them died —
this one goes out
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the widow. She is free and does not need יבום.

phrases.english: because she is a wife's sister.
And the same for two deaf-mute women.
An adult and a minor,
and the husband of the minor died —
the minor goes out
because she is a wife's sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁנֵי אַחִין נְשׂוּאִין לִשְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת קְטַנּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous sugya about רבי אלעזר's view ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the widow's marriage was only rabbinic (two minors, two deaf-mutes, or the minor's husband died), she goes out as אחות אשה without יבום.

steps.title: The adult's husband died: teach the minor to refuse
steps.stepSummary: When the adult sister's husband dies, רבי אליעזר says we teach the living brother's minor wife to do מיאון, so that he can do יבום with the adult widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the husband of the adult died, רבי אליעזר says: we teach the minor to refuse him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now reaches the hard case, where the widow is an adult. רבי אליעזר gives the first opinion: we actively guide the minor wife to refuse her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the widow's bond of יבום comes from the Torah, while the living brother's marriage to the minor is only rabbinic. If the minor does מיאון, her marriage is undone, she is no longer his wife, and he is free to do יבום with her adult sister.

keyTerms.meaning: An adult woman; her marriage is fully valid by Torah law
We teach or instruct
Refusal: a minor girl's declaration that she does not want her husband, which undoes the rabbinic marriage

phrases.english: If the husband of the adult died,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
We teach the minor
to refuse him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is her own husband, the living brother. Once she refuses, he can do יבום with her sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת בַּעְלָהּ שֶׁל גְּדוֹלָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the easy cases to the hard case, where the adult sister is the widow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: we instruct the minor wife to do מיאון so the Torah-level יבום can happen.

steps.title: Do not push her; if she does not refuse, wait until she grows up
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says we do not push the minor to refuse. If she refuses on her own, fine; if not, we wait until she becomes an adult, and then the widow goes out as אחות אשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: If she refused, she refused. And if not, the widow waits until the minor grows up, and then that widow goes out because she is a wife's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל disagrees with רבי אליעזר. He accepts a refusal if it happens, but we do not teach her to do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the minor does not refuse, we wait for her to grow up. Then her marriage becomes fully valid by Torah law, so the adult widow is truly his wife's sister and is exempt from יבום. The difference from רבי אליעזר is whether we push the minor to refuse.

keyTerms.meaning: If she refused, her refusal stands; it is accepted but not encouraged
She shall wait
Until she grows up and becomes an adult

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
If she refused — she refused,
phrases.notes: Meaning: if the minor refuses on her own, it works, but we do not tell her to.

phrases.english: and if not —
she [the widow] waits until [the minor] grows up,
and that one goes out
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the adult widow, not the minor wife.

phrases.english: because she is a wife's sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר אִם מֵיאֲנָה מֵיאֲנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion on the same case, disagreeing with רבי אליעזר about teaching the minor to refuse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל: a refusal is valid if she does it herself; otherwise wait until she is an adult, and then the widow is exempt as אחות אשה.

steps.title: Woe to him: he loses both women
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says the living brother loses both: he must divorce his minor wife with a גט and do חליצה with his brother's widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: Woe to him over his wife, and woe to him over his brother's wife! He sends away his wife with a גט, and his brother's wife with חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives a third, stricter opinion for the case where the adult's husband died. The living brother ends up losing both women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He cannot stay married to his minor wife, because she is the sister of a woman bound to him by Torah-level יבום. He cannot do יבום with the widow either, because she is his wife's sister. Her rabbinic marriage is not strong enough to make the widow a full ערוה who is totally exempt, so he must divorce his wife and do חליצה with the widow.

keyTerms.meaning: Woe to him: a cry over his loss
His brother's wife, here the widow waiting for יבום
A bill of divorce
The ceremony that releases a widow from יבום

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on the adult widow: רבי אליעזר says teach the minor to refuse; רבן גמליאל says accept a refusal if it comes, otherwise wait until she grows up; רבי יהושע says he loses both, with a גט for his wife and חליצה for the widow.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
Woe to him over his wife,
woe to him over his brother's wife.
He sends away his wife with a bill of divorce —
and his brother's wife with חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר אִי לוֹ עַל אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third opinion on the adult-widow case, stricter than both רבי אליעזר and רבן גמליאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע: the living brother must divorce his minor wife with a גט and release the widow with חליצה.

steps.title: How can we tell the minor to refuse when בר קפרא says to stay away from refusal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's ruling to teach the minor to do מיאון. בר קפרא taught that a person should stay away from מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Is that really allowed? Didn't בר קפרא teach that a person should always hold on to three things and stay away from three things? Hold on to חליצה, bringing peace, and annulling vows. Stay away from מיאון, deposits, and being a guarantor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי אליעזר from the משנה, who said we teach the minor to do מיאון. It brings a ברייתא that says to stay away from מיאון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר actively pushes for a מיאון so the brother can do יבום. But בר קפרא lists מיאון among the things a person should avoid. So how can we deliberately cause one?

keyTerms.meaning: And is it permitted? An opening that introduces a challenge
He should cling to, or hold on to
He should distance himself from
Deposits, meaning items left with someone to guard
Being a guarantor for someone else's loan
Annulling vows

phrases.english: GEMARA: And is it permitted?
phrases.notes: He means: is it allowed to teach the minor to refuse, the way רבי אליעזר said?

phrases.english: But didn't בר קפרא teach:
A person should always cling to three things,
and distance himself from three things.
He should cling to three things:
to חליצה, to bringing peace, and to annulling vows.
And he should distance himself from three things:

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַמֵּיאוּן, וּמִן הַפִּקְדוֹנוֹת, וּמִן הָעֵרְבוֹנוֹת!
phrases.english: from refusal, from deposits, and from being a guarantor!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אליעזר's ruling in the משנה (step 24).
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's instruction to teach the minor to do מיאון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says to stay away from מיאון, so actively encouraging one seems wrong.

steps.title: A refusal done for a מצוה is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a מיאון done to make a מצוה possible is not included in the warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: A refusal done for the sake of a מצוה is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. בר קפרא's warning does not apply when the מיאון helps a מצוה happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the minor's מיאון removes the אחות אשה problem. That lets the living brother do the מצוה of יבום with the widow. בר קפרא's general warning is about an ordinary מיאון, not one that serves a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: A refusal done for the sake of a מצוה
Is different

phrases.english: A refusal for a מצוה is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every מיאון should be avoided, so רבי אליעזר's advice seems improper.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a מיאון that is not for a מצוה is discouraged. This one allows יבום, so it is fine.
steps.whatToRemember: בר קפרא says to stay away from מיאון. But a מיאון that makes a מצוה possible is an exception.

steps.title: Explaining 'cling to חליצה' through the view of אבא שאול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to בר קפרא's teaching to explain it. Preferring חליצה follows אבא שאול, who says that doing יבום for personal reasons is almost like a forbidden relationship.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the teaching itself. בר קפרא taught: A person should always hold on to three things. First, חליצה, which follows אבא שאול. As a ברייתא teaches, אבא שאול says: Someone who marries his יבמה for her beauty, for the sake of marriage, or for any other reason is as if he has relations with an ערוה. To me it seems almost as if the child would be a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to explain בר קפרא's list one item at a time. It starts with why a person should prefer חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Preferring חליצה over יבום matches the view of אבא שאול. He holds that יבום must be done only for the sake of the מצוה. If a man does יבום for her looks, for marriage, or for any other benefit, it is close to a forbidden relationship. So the safer choice is חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself. Used when the גמרא goes back to examine a source it just quoted
For the sake of her beauty
For the sake of being married to her
Having relations with a woman forbidden to him
A child born from a forbidden relationship

steps.confusionAlert: אבא שאול does not say the child really is a ממזר. He says it is close to that in his eyes. This is strong language meant to discourage יבום for the wrong reasons.

phrases.english: The matter itself.
בר קפרא taught:
A person should always cling to three things:
to חליצה, in line with אבא שאול,
as a ברייתא teaches, אבא שאול says:
One who marries his יבמה for her beauty,
for the sake of marriage, or for some other reason,
it is as if he has relations with a forbidden woman,
and in my eyes the child is close to being a ממזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא quoted in step 27 to explain its parts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Preferring חליצה follows אבא שאול, who considers יבום for personal motives close to a forbidden relationship.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a central source for the debate over whether חליצה or יבום is preferred.

steps.title: Cling to bringing peace, based on a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The second item, bringing peace, comes from the פסוק 'Seek peace and pursue it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Bringing peace: as it is written, 'Seek peace and pursue it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second item on בר קפרא's list. It gives a פסוק as the source for chasing after peace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not just say to look for peace when it comes your way. It says to pursue it. That is why a person should actively hold on to bringing peace.

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing peace between people
And pursue it

phrases.english: To bringing peace, as it is written:
"Seek peace and pursue it,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the second item in בר קפרא's list.
